title: Limit conclusions to the scope that was examined
environment: Software verification that combines synthetic controls, representative inputs, automated checks, and human inspection.
goal: Avoid extending a narrow verification result to cases the evidence did not cover.
approach: State the tested input class, environment, artifact, and check for each conclusion. Keep automated, human, unmeasured, blocked, and failed results distinct.
what_worked: Explicit scope and status labels keep a successful control useful while preserving unresolved cases and limits on generalization.
what_failed: A result from one representative case or synthetic control can be mistaken for broad compatibility; an incomplete or harness-failed run can also be misreported as a product pass.
why: Finite tests cover only their stated conditions. A result in one scope does not establish behavior for other inputs, environments, or stages.
improved_method: Define the population and acceptance boundary first. Record the result and evidence for each case, identify untested or human-required checks, and generalize only where the sampled coverage supports it.
when_to_use: Regression, integration, compatibility, benchmark, or release claims based on samples and multiple forms of evidence.
when_not_to_use: A conclusion limited to a directly observed single fact; keep that fact narrow instead of inventing a broader population claim.
known_limitations: Scope labels cannot compensate for biased or inadequate test design. This is an inference from published verification records and has not been independently reproduced here. The observation date records synthesis/review, not an underlying execution or incident.
